name: LangSmith Sandboxes

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Max 1 seat. 'Limited to 10 Sandboxes' (count of sandboxes, not explicitly running only; stopped sandboxes are kept 14 days by default and may count). Pay-as-you-go after adding a card. 5 LCU + 1 LSU sandbox allowance per month. Restricted egress (managed allowlist) by default.

plans.name: Plus (one seat)
plans.note: $39 per seat per month. A seat is every distinct user, including invited users. Seats are prorated when added, with no credit when removed. No published sandbox count cap. Marketing says 'Burst to thousands on demand ... without rate limits or queueing'. Includes 10k base traces and 1 free small serverless deployment. Restricted egress by default for non-Enterprise orgs.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

caveats: Public list rates are expressed in LCU and LSU. $1.50/LCU and $1/LSU; CPU 0.0384 LCU/vCPU-h, RAM 0.0123 LCU/GiB-h, storage 0.000123 LSU/GiB-h. Credits are separate compute and storage pools, not fungible dollars.
Storage meter scope versus retained filesystem snapshot pricing needs invoice confirmation.
Plus concurrency and maximum sandbox size not stated on pricing page.

ENGINE_CARD cannot apply all independent free CPU/RAM/storage/request allowances exactly. Raw regimes/worked example retain them; any engine subtotal may overstate charges or miss eligibility. Do not subtract them twice.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
No SSH/desktop/browser product documented (2026-09-28); access is via SDK exec, file APIs, service URLs and TCP tunnels. A browser could be installed in a custom image, but none is provided.

Restricted egress by default for non-Enterprise orgs: only a managed allowlist (PyPI, npm, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, LangSmith, mostly HTTPS:443). Unrestricted egress needs a support-ticket exemption.
Enterprise is invoiced annually upfront and LCUs draw down committed LangChain credits. Startups can get up to $10,000 in credits (application program).
New organisations created manually must be on Plus. Developer is only the personal org.
CPU bursts to 2x requested when the host has spare capacity. It is not documented whether burst CPU is billed; the billed allocation is presumably the requested vCPU.

fleet.tiers: Developer limited to 10 sandboxes; Plus raises access, but numeric paid cap not stated; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Pricing says 10 Sandboxes without fully clarifying retained versus running count. Count recorded conservatively as upper bound; no verified 50/300/1,000 entitlement inferred from scale-to-thousands marketing.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: preserve_memory_on_stop | true suspends RAM on a voluntary stop (idle timeout or explicit stop) so the sandbox resumes where it left off when it next wakes, rather than cold-booting. Defaults to false, which keeps only the filesystem. Restarts triggered by infrastructure maintenance preserve memory either way.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in per sandbox at create time (REST API field; not yet in Python/TS SDK). Trigger: idle timeout (idle_ttl_seconds, default 600 s) or explicit stop; memory + running processes included; wake is automatic on next exec/file/service-URL request. Default (false) keeps only the filesystem across stop, which is persistent_disk, not this. Stopped sandboxes are deleted after delete_after_stop_seconds (default ~14 days, max 30).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can also capture a snapshot from a running sandbox—install packages, write data files, or configure state, then snapshot the result and reuse it as a new starting point.
snapshot_on_demand.note: SDK sb.capture_snapshot(name) / CLI `langsmith sandbox snapshot capture` / REST POST /api/v2/sandboxes/boxes/{name}/snapshot. Filesystem-only by default; REST `include_memory: true` also captures RAM ('Boot from one and the sandbox resumes where it left off, with its processes still running'), running or stopped sandbox; not supported on overlay-rootfs sandboxes (LangSmith assigns runtime). New sandboxes boot from the snapshot by id or name (template/fork).

harness_api.quote: Deep Agents Code uses the sandbox as tool pattern: the dcode process (LLM loop, memory, tool dispatch) runs on your machine, but agent tool calls (read_file, write_file, execute, etc.) target the remote sandbox
harness_api.note: LangChain's own agents (Deep Agents Code, Managed Deep Agents on Agent Server, which has thread/run APIs) run OUTSIDE the sandbox and use it as a tool backend. The Deep Agents docs describe an 'agent in sandbox' pattern but say 'you have to add additional infrastructure to handle communication between your application and the agent inside the sandbox' - no first-party API for driving Claude Code/Codex/etc. inside a LangSmith sandbox. Sandbox API is exec/stream/files/tunnel only. Borderline: if the coordinator counts Managed Deep Agents (public beta, US only) as a harness API, flip to true with that caveat.

egress_allowlist.quote: allow_list | Default-deny. Only listed destinations are reachable, on any protocol. List every host the sandbox needs, including the HTTP(S) hosts your rules and callbacks target.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox proxy_config.access_control allow_list or deny_list; 'Access control is enforced per connection on the sandbox host'. Patterns: host, host:PORT, *.glob, ~regex, literal IP (with port), CIDR - but IP/CIDR entries only affect cleartext HTTP on port 80 (raw TCP/HTTPS to literal IPs is dropped), so in practice domain+port. Only TCP leaves (UDP/QUIC/ICMP dropped). Non-Enterprise orgs are on a LangSmith-managed restricted-egress allowlist by default (PyPI, npm, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, LangSmith); unrestricted needs a support ticket. Private/loopback/metadata addresses always refused.

egress_http_rules.quote: full_request | When true, every request to a matched host invokes the callback (nothing is cached) and the body includes a request snapshot: method, url, scheme, host, path, query, headers, and up to 1 MiB of the body as body_base64
egress_http_rules.note: No declarative method/path allow/deny. HTTP-level control exists via (a) header-injection rules with match_hosts + match_paths, and (b) callbacks: the proxy POSTs the full request (method/path/headers/body) to your endpoint and 'Any non-2xx response ... fails closed: the sandbox's request is rejected with 502' - so your callback can enforce arbitrary per-request policy. HTTPS to matched hosts is MITM-decrypted by the proxy (sandbox trusts its CA).

ingress_rules.quote: Tokens are short-lived (default 10 minutes, max 24 hours) and there is no server-side refresh mechanism.
ingress_rules.note: Ports are reachable only via authenticated service URLs (per sandbox+port, X-Langsmith-Sandbox-Service-Token / browser token; share links work for anyone holding the link until expiry) or API-key-authenticated TCP tunnels (`langsmith sandbox tunnel`). No public IPs, no IP allowlists documented. Sandbox permissions control which workspace members can interact with a sandbox.

guest_firewall.quote: Sandbox runtime pods that run sandbox workloads on KVM-capable nodes.
guest_firewall.note: KVM microVMs (self-host requires /dev/kvm) with an Ubuntu 24.04 ext4 root filesystem and root access (setup scripts run apt-get). Not documented explicitly; derived. Rules inside would sit behind the host-side egress proxy.

secret_proxy.quote: When configured on a sandbox, an egress proxy running outside the sandbox automatically injects authentication headers into matching outbound requests using your workspace secrets or write-only credentials you provide in the proxy config.
secret_proxy.note: Arbitrary hosts via header rules (workspace_secret / write-only opaque values; placeholders via env_vars), dynamic credentials via signed callbacks, built-in AWS SigV4 signing (static keys or IAM role) and GCP service-account token minting; git over HTTPS works (GitHub example uses Basic auth header). Non-HTTP (PostgreSQL, SSH, Redis) 'passes through unchanged' - no injection for non-HTTP protocols.

volume_attach.quote: Sandbox mounts attach external data sources to a sandbox filesystem when the sandbox is created. Use mounts when sandbox code needs direct file access to object storage buckets, public Git repositories, or Context Hub repos without copying the data into the sandbox image.
volume_attach.note: No first-party block/network volume product: the sandbox API has boxes, snapshots, registries, files, tunnels, service URLs but no volume resource. Storage is the per-sandbox root filesystem (resizable via --rootfs-capacity / fs_capacity_bytes). Extra storage only via mounts of customer-owned S3/GCS buckets (FUSE-style VFS cache, read-write or read-only), public Git repos and read-only Context Hub repos - see volume_shared.

volume_shared.quote: For writable mounts, keep writeback_seconds low when another process needs to read the objects from S3 or GCS soon after the sandbox writes them.
volume_shared.note: First-party mount feature for customer-owned S3/GCS buckets (read_only true/false; writable mounts write back to the bucket), plus Git (clone) and Context Hub (read-only, one-way sync) mounts. The same bucket/prefix can be mounted by several sandboxes (bucket is 'the source of truth'), but it is object storage with a local cache and writeback delay, not a POSIX shared filesystem; concurrent multi-sandbox mounting is not stated explicitly. Mounts are set at sandbox creation.
